skills.name: Reasons for African cooperation with Europeans

note.text: African cooperation with European actors could be motivated by trade, security, political rivalry, diplomacy, access to education or an attempt to preserve authority under pressure. It did not necessarily mean endorsement of permanent colonial domination. Local actors made choices in unequal and changing circumstances. Some cooperated in one matter while resisting another. Explain a specific actor's situation rather than assigning one motive to all Africans or judging a choice without examining the available alternatives.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: African cooperation with European actors could be motivated by trade, security, political rivalry, diplomacy, access to education or an attempt to preserve authority under pressure. It did not necessarily mean endorsement of permanent colonial domination. Local actors made choices in unequal and changing circumstances. Some cooperated in one matter while resisting another. Explain a specific actor's situation rather than assigning one motive to all Africans or judging a choice without examining the available alternatives.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A ruler facing a local rival might seek an outside alliance; a trader might seek access to a commercial network. A community may negotiate to reduce immediate harm rather than welcome every imposed demand. These original analytical examples illustrate possible motives, not invented quotations attributed to historical chiefs.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the desired benefit, the pressure and the risks. Ask whether cooperation concerned one project or the entire political relationship. Separate an explanation of a decision from moral approval of its consequences. Use local evidence before assigning a named leader a particular motive.
